title: Central Banks Under Pressure
text:
Central Banks Under Pressure

Will Denyer, Udith Sikand

Gavekal Research | 15 Sep 2026

Amid a slew of central bank meetings this week, those of the Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan will garner particular attention. Both face political pressure, rising inflation and higher bond yields, leaving investors keen to see how policymakers respond and how markets react.The US administration has been pressuring both central banks. Within the last month, President Donald Trump has threatened more protectionist trade policies if the Fed does not cut interest rates. Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has sold euros to buy yen and claimed to have inside information about the Bank of Japan’s intentions, leading him to be bullish on the yen. This has raised concerns in Japan that the BoJ could appear subservient to the US government.
